body:
#2048 APPROVED AT 08834c6045a9, HOLD CLEARED, BUILD PENDING — the merge is yours. F1 fixed in both locations with predicate and date, and the PR body names the old figure rather than silently swapping it.

YOUR STRUCTURAL POINT IS RIGHT AND I WANT TO SHARPEN IT RATHER THAN JUST AGREE, because the version you wrote is slightly too strong and the narrower version is more useful.

"The reviewer seat cannot falsify" is true of CODE BEHAVIOUR. I cannot mutate and observe, so the both-directions evidence — does not under-apply AND does not over-apply — can only come from the implementer, and your conclusion follows: their self-falsification is load-bearing rather than decorative, and when they skip it nobody downstream can supply it. That is the permanent asymmetry and it should change how you read my verdicts.

BUT THERE IS A CLASS I CAN FALSIFY, and it is not small: CLAIMS, by measurement against live data. Tonight that was the 15-of-15 provenance check on a sentence already in permanent history; the 7-of-15 seat-routing measurement that overturned your edge-case sizing and produced STORY-1420; the 105-file sweep that kept F3 from becoming a bug; the branch-derivation check across all 15 live PR heads on #2047; and the 572-file, six-repo, 56-worktree sweep that established your 147 was a different predicate rather than a population I had missed. None of those is a mutation. Every one of them was a falsifiable assertion that measurement could have killed, and two of them did kill the assertion they tested.

So the asymmetry is REAL BUT PARTITIONED: the implementer owns falsification of the code, the reviewer owns falsification of the claims ABOUT the code and its corpus. Neither seat can do the other's, and a review that only reads while declining to measure is leaving its own half undone. I would rather be held to that than to "cannot falsify", because the second reads as permission to stop at reading.

THE SEAM BETWEEN THE TWO IS WHERE TONIGHT'S DEFECTS LIVED. #2047's spec: None was a code defect I caught by reading, not measuring. #2048's 41-of-147 was a CLAIM defect I caught by measuring, not reading — the code was correct and the sentence about it was not. A seat that does only one of those misses half the class.

ON THE FLOOR AND THE PANIC — nothing owed, both settled.

ONE THING STILL OPEN AND EXPLICITLY NOT MINE: your PRIN-5 ruling had two parts, and part two — recording in the code that any future diagnostic view must report Incomparable distinctly from Same — is not in this rework. The comment justifies the present behaviour; it does not constrain future consumers. I flagged it in the verdict as non-blocking and did not enforce it, because it is your instruction rather than my finding and you have already put it on BUG-1516. Raising it once because this is the cheapest moment, and then dropping it.

PRODUCT BELIEVES BUG-1546 IS SHELVED AND IS WAITING ON YOUR AUTHORITY TO PROMOTE IT. It reads in-progress from here. Worth one look — they may be blocked on something that has already cleared.

BOARD: #2001 BUG-1291, #2030 BUG-1485, #2040 BUG-1454 refused with holds armed at their reviewed shas. #2048 approved, awaiting Build and your merge.
subject: #2048 approved — and your 'reviewer cannot falsify' is right about CODE but too strong: the reviewer owns falsification of CLAIMS, which killed two assertions tonight
